examples.en: One way or the other, please give me an answer today.

examples.ko: 가부간 결정이 나야 다음 일을 진행할 수 있어요.
examples.en: We can move on to the next task only after a yes-or-no decision.

examples.ko: 초대에 갈 수 있는지 가부간에 연락 주세요.
examples.en: Please let me know yes or no on whether you can come to the invitation.

examples.ko: 일이 되든 안 되든 가부간에 결과는 알려 줄게요.
examples.en: Whether it works out or not, I will tell you the result.

examples.ko: 사장님이 가부간에 아무 말씀이 없어서 답답해요.
examples.en: The boss has said neither yes nor no, so I feel frustrated.

examples.ko: 이번 주 안에 가부간 소식을 듣고 싶어요.
examples.en: I would like to hear a yes or no by the end of this week.

explain: '된다/안 된다' 중 어느 쪽이든 답을 달라고 할 때 써요. 보통 '가부간에 답을 주다, 가부간에 연락하다'처럼 말해요. 회사나 공식적인 말에 어울리고, 친구끼리는 '된다 안 된다 말해 줘'처럼 풀어서 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when asking for an answer of either 'yes' or 'no'. It usually appears as '가부간에 답을 주다' or '가부간에 연락하다'. It suits work or formal speech, and among friends people just say something like '된다 안 된다 말해 줘'.

en: dismissal (of a legal claim or petition)

examples.en: The court dismissed this lawsuit.
The application was rejected because of missing documents.
A decision to dismiss this case was issued.

examples.ko: 변호사는 각하를 받아들일 수 없다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The lawyer said he couldn't accept the dismissal.

examples.ko: 항소가 각하 판결을 받아서 다시 준비해야 해요.
examples.en: The appeal got a dismissal ruling, so we have to prepare again.
Please check what the reason for the dismissal is.

explain: 법원이나 관청에서 신청이나 소송을 들어보지 않고 돌려보낼 때 쓰는 법률 용어예요. 내용을 보고 '안 된다'고 하는 '기각'과 달라요. 대통령에게 쓰던 높임말 '각하'와 소리만 같고 뜻은 전혀 달라요.
explain_en: It is a legal term for when a court or office turns away a claim without examining its substance, which differs from 기각 (rejecting after review). It shares only its sound with the old honorific 각하 once used for presidents.

en: to be rejected; to be dismissed

examples.en: The application was dismissed because of incomplete documents.

examples.ko: 소송이 각하되면 처음부터 다시 해야 해요.
examples.en: If the lawsuit is dismissed, you have to start over.
I'm worried that the claim will be dismissed.

examples.ko: 각하된 사건은 다시 접수할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A dismissed case can be filed again.
I got word that the objection was dismissed.
It ended up being dismissed because the deadline had passed.

explain: 법원이나 관청이 신청이나 소송을 내용도 보지 않고 돌려보낼 때 써요. 서류가 빠졌거나 기한을 넘겼을 때 자주 일어나고, 내용을 보고 거절하는 '기각되다'와 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when a court or office returns a petition or lawsuit without examining its content, often due to missing documents or a missed deadline. It differs from 기각되다, where the content is reviewed and then rejected.

examples.en: The government revised the law.
The publisher will revise the book.
The school decided to revise its rules.
Revising takes a long time.
We posted the revised content on the website.

examples.ko: 회사가 이용 약관을 개정하고 사용자에게 알렸어요.
examples.en: The company revised its terms of use and notified users.

explain: '고치다'는 틀린 것도 낡은 물건도 고치지만, '개정하다'는 법·규칙·약관 같은 문서의 내용을 공식적으로 바꿀 때만 써요. 하는 쪽은 정부나 회사 같은 곳이에요. 일상 대화에서 '내 계획을 개정했어요'라고는 하지 않아요.
explain_en: '고치다' fixes mistakes and old things, but '개정하다' is only for officially changing documents such as laws, rules, or terms. The one doing it is a body like a government or company. In daily talk you would not say '내 계획을 개정했어요'.

en: erasure; striking off a record or registration

examples.ko: 폐차하면 자동차 등록 말소를 신청해야 해요.
examples.en: If you scrap a car, you have to apply to cancel its registration.

examples.ko: 오래 쓰지 않은 계정은 말소될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Accounts that haven't been used for a long time can be deleted.
If your resident registration is cancelled, there are many inconveniences.

examples.ko: 사업자 등록 말소 때문에 세무서에 다녀왔어요.
examples.en: I went to the tax office because of the cancellation of my business registration.

examples.ko: 잘못 올라간 기록은 말소 처리를 요청하세요.
examples.en: Please request that wrongly entered records be struck from the file.
I was shocked because my name had been struck from the list.

explain: 등록, 기록, 이름을 지워서 없앤다는 뜻이라 '등록 말소'처럼 행정이나 법 이야기에서 써요. '말소리'(말하는 소리)와는 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is about wiping out a registration, record or name, so it appears in administrative and legal talk, as in '등록 말소' (registration cancellation). It is a completely different word from '말소리' (the sound of speech).

examples.en: The court issued a warrant.

examples.ko: 경찰은 교통 위반 고지서를 발부하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are issuing traffic violation notices.
The district office did not issue the permit.
The judge carefully decides whether to issue a warrant.
To issue a warrant, a legal reason is required.
Be sure to keep the documents issued by the agency.

explain: 영장·고지서·허가증처럼 기관이 공식적으로 내주는 것에 써요. 학교나 회사에서 증명서를 떼어 주는 일에는 '발급하다'를 더 많이 써요. 책·돈·신문을 내놓는 일은 '발행하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for things an institution officially hands out, such as warrants, notices and permits. For certificates from a school or company, '발급하다' is used more. Putting out books, money or newspapers is '발행하다'.

en: to be granted; to be given

examples.en: Every student is given a number.
A lot of responsibility was given to this job.
Members will be granted a discount benefit.

examples.ko: 권한이 부여된 사람만 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who have been given permission can enter.

examples.ko: 새 계정에는 임시 비밀번호가 부여되고 있어요.
examples.en: Temporary passwords are being issued to new accounts.
A special mission was assigned to the player.

explain: '받다'보다 딱딱해서 공문, 규칙, 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 번호·권한·자격·책임·의미처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 주어지는 경우가 많아서, 선물이나 돈에는 '받다'를 써요. 주는 쪽은 '부여하다'예요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '받다' and shows up in official notices, rules and news. It is usually for intangible things such as numbers, authority, qualifications or meaning; for gifts or money Koreans use 받다. The giver's verb is 부여하다.

examples.en: I heard this review council will meet next week.
This agenda item has to go through the review council.

examples.ko: 심의회 위원들이 새 규정을 검토하고 있어요.
examples.en: The council members are reviewing the new regulations.
The review council approved the screening of that film.
The council also heard the citizens' opinions directly.
The city hall announced the results of the council's review.

explain: 안건을 자세히 따져 보고 의견을 내거나 결정하는 모임이에요. '위원회'와 비슷하게 쓰지만 '심의회'는 이름에서 심의하는 일이 중심이라는 것이 드러나요. 뉴스나 공문서에서 'OO 심의회' 형태로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a body that examines agenda items closely and gives opinions or decisions. It is similar to '위원회', but the name '심의회' shows that deliberation is its main role. It often appears in news and official documents in the form 'OO 심의회'.

examples.en: The bank clerk told me to bring my registered seal.

examples.ko: 집을 살 때 인감도장이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: You absolutely need a registered seal when buying a house.
I lost my registered seal, so I had a new one made.
You must not lend your registered seal to just anyone.
I went to the community center and registered my seal.
Please stamp your registered seal on this document.

explain: 미리 관청에 등록해 두고 중요한 계약이나 서류에 쓰는 도장이라 평소에 쓰는 '막도장'과 달라요. 줄여서 '인감'이라고도 하고, 도장이 맞는지 증명하는 서류는 '인감증명서'예요.
explain_en: This is a seal registered in advance with the authorities and used for important contracts and documents, unlike an everyday '막도장'. It is often shortened to '인감', and the document proving it is genuine is the '인감증명서'.

examples.en: The manager has the discretion to decide on refunds.
The person in charge made a decision that went beyond their discretion.

examples.ko: 이건 제 재량권 밖이라서 팀장님께 여쭤볼게요.
examples.en: This is outside my authority, so I'll ask the team leader.
There is a lot of discretion, but the responsibility is just as great.

examples.ko: 현장 직원에게 재량권도 주어야 손님 응대가 빨라져요.
examples.en: You need to give on-site staff discretion too so that customers are served faster.

examples.ko: 재량권 때문에 지점마다 규칙이 조금씩 달라요.
examples.en: Because of discretionary power, the rules differ slightly at each branch.

explain: 규정만 따르지 않고 자기 판단으로 정할 수 있는 권한이에요. 직장, 학교, 관공서 이야기에서 쓰고 '재량권이 있다/없다', '재량권을 주다'처럼 말해요. '제 재량으로 처리할게요'처럼 '재량'만 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the authority to decide using your own judgment rather than strictly following rules. It appears in talk about workplaces, schools and government offices, as in '재량권이 있다/없다' or '재량권을 주다'. You can also use just '재량', as in '제 재량으로 처리할게요'.
